validity.recommendation: no change to existence/classification; row is well-documented and correctly classified
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: extensively and independently documented, not a GEM-only entity. Announced 4 Dec 2017 by the Liberty Utilities Group (a Algonquin Power & Utilities Corp subsidiary) per Algonquin's own SEC Form 40-F FY2017 AIF (primary corporate disclosure, sec.gov, verified). Independently covered start-to-finish by NHPR, Seacoastonline, the Union Leader, InDepthNH, and the Pipeline & Gas Journal 'Planned Projects' trade listing (Oct 2018 / rev. Jul 2018) -- five independent origins spanning trade press, regional press, public radio and the sponsor's own regulatory filing. Went through a real NH PUC docket and Site Evaluation Committee review (2017-2020), drew organized opposition (350NH, ECHO Action), and was formally abandoned by Liberty in a PUC filing on 31 Jul 2020. No trace of fabrication; this is a real proposed-then-cancelled project. CLASSIFICATION: correctly classified as a gas transmission pipeline (Fuel=Gas) -- every independent source describes an underground steel natural-gas transmission line connecting two interstate pipeline systems (Tennessee Gas Pipeline at Manchester; PNGTS/Maritimes & Northeast at the Seacoast end), not a gathering, process or distribution line. Not a duplicate of any other US-gas-batch roster row -- no other roster PID touches New Hampshire or this corridor. CAVEAT: Capacity (pipe throughput, MMcf/d), Pressure/MAOP and FuelSource could not be sourced -- see the corresponding fills[] UNRESOLVED records for what was searched and why. The project never reached FERC certification or final engineering, so a published throughput-capacity or MAOP figure independent of GEM likely does not exist for this line; the only capacity figure in any source (2 Bcf) is the SEPARATE Epping LNG storage tank's storage capacity, not pipe flow capacity, and was not force-fit into the Capacity field (aggregate/wrong-unit rule).

validity.recommendation: verify the Seacoast-end interconnect town before pasting a fixed spelling for EndLocation -- do not just correct 'Exter' to 'Exeter' without resolving this
validity.researcher_notes: The sheet's EndLocation reads 'Exter' (an evident typo, presumably meaning Exeter, NH), and independent sources genuinely split on which Seacoast-area town the pipeline actually terminated at. FOUR independent sources -- including the sponsor's own primary disclosure -- name STRATHAM as the Seacoast-end interconnect: (1) Algonquin Power & Utilities Corp's own SEC Form 40-F FY2017 AIF: 'the proposed Granite Bridge project would connect the existing Portland Natural Gas Transmission System and Maritimes and Northeast Pipeline facilities in Stratham with the existing Tennessee Gas Pipeline facilities in Manchester'; (2) NHPR: 'run about 27 miles along Route 101 between Stratham and Manchester'; (3) Pipeline & Gas Journal 'Planned Projects' (rev. 7/18): 'Location: Manchester, NH - Stratham, NH'; (4) InDepthNH (31 Jul 2020): '16-inch-wide steel underground pipeline that would run 27 miles, from Stratham to Manchester.' TWO independent sources instead name EXETER: Seacoastonline (17 Mar 2019): 'The proposed underground 27-mile, 16-inch diameter pipeline from Manchester to Exeter,' plus detail that Liberty held an easement with the TOWN of Exeter to build a metering station there; and the Union Leader (1 Aug 2020): 'would have followed Route 101 to bring natural gas from Exeter to Manchester.' Reading Seacoastonline closely resolves part of the puzzle without fully closing it: the Select Board minutes it cites say that had Exeter rejected the metering-station easement, 'Liberty would've been forced to build its metering station in Stratham' -- i.e. Stratham was the fallback site for a METERING STATION along the route, while the pipeline's actual upstream interconnect with PNGTS/M&NE (per Liberty's own SEC filing) was in Stratham. It is plausible the two press accounts naming Exeter are describing the metering-station host town rather than the pipeline's true end-of-line interconnect, but I could not find a single source stating both facts explicitly enough to settle it with certainty. Given the sponsor's own regulatory filing plus three more independent accounts say Stratham, EndLocation is more likely Stratham than Exeter; flagging as a spec/attribution concern rather than silently overwriting, since two independent regional papers do say Exeter. StartLocation=Manchester is undisputed across every source.
